set.st: Joseph Oesterle came from Le Havre in 1849, had a log cabin and trading post on Oesterle Lake and built up about 1,000 acres in east Sharon township (over 800 acres on the 1876 plat; the 1856 pre-emption in sec. 26 T25N was other land); the 1895 plat shows his 240 acres across the S half of sec. 3 T24N R9E, by Oesterle Lake. After he died in the 1890s, Albert Steiner, an orphan raised by the family, said he had seen Joseph bury gold in the cellar of the frame house; Mrs. August Oesterle dug and found rusted cans of gold coins, and her daughter counted $2,500 in fives, tens and twenties. Whether every can was found is unknown.
set.pl: Oesterle homestead on Oesterle Lake, S half sec 3 T24N R9E, Sharon Twp (1895 plat); the 1856 pre-emption in sec 26 was other land
